newsitem.title: SPAIN: Albright urges Cambodia factions to make peace.
newsitem.headline: Albright urges Cambodia factions to make peace.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright reacted cautiously on Monday to fighting in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh, calling on the rival factions to settle their differences peacefully.

At a news conference, Albright declined direct comment on reports that Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen had taken complete control of Phnom Penh and its outskirts, ousting his rival Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"What we believe is important is that the various contending parties solve their problems through peaceful means and not military means," said Albright, who is in Madrid for a NATO summit on Tuesday.

Albright, who cancelled a planned visit to Cambodia last month because of the tensions there, said she expected that the international community would be "considering the subject in more official ways", but she did not elaborate.

"The international community has a great amount invested in making sure that there is a peaceful dialogue there and that the people of Cambodia are not yet again victims of fighting among various factions," she added.
Albright expressed sympathy for the people of Cambodia who she said had hoped that 1993 elections would bring peace to their war-ravaged country.

Hun Sen formerly led a Vietnamese-backed government in Cambodia. First Prime Minister Ranariddh, who is in France, heads the royalist FUNCINPEC party. The two have been uneasy coalition partners since 1993.
